Houston, Clint Coley is behind the Rent’s Due podcast, where he shares the work of building his next special.

His comedy is candid, blunt, and built for a live room. He talks relationships, Philly culture, and the real parts of mental health with high-energy storytelling. If you like comedy that feels like an honest conversation, bring a friend.

Punch Line Houston · Thursday, November 12, 2026

Houston, Ellen Skrmetti was a guest on *That Sounds Fun with Annie F. Downs*, and she’s headed your way.

Her comedy is clean, Southern, and built from real life: faith, family, marriage, motherhood, and midlife. She began performing in 2020 after taking writing classes at 41, and now tells the kind of personal stories you’ll recognize before the punchline lands. I’d go for the honest point of view and bring someone who appreciates a good Southern observation.

Houston Improv · Thursday, November 12, 2026

Houston, you may know Reem Edan from her Dry Bar Comedy special, *Ethnic, Ambiguous & Single*.

I’d see her live for the sharp, unfiltered way she talks about Iraqi-American life, Muslim upbringing, family, and dating. She mixes stand-up with character work, so the stories have extra bite. She also performed in Arabic on Shahid VIP’s *The Stand Up Sketch Show*.

Houston, you may know Chrissy Chlapecka from her 2021 appearance on Craig & Friends.

She brings colorful, theatrical, vocal-forward pop shows with high-camp, hyper-feminine energy and politically pointed humor. Her new 16-track album, *Christine: High Voltage*, is the second act of her *Christine* project. If you like pop performance with queer joy and something to say, put this on your list.
